 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Sacramento Kings take a break from their seven-game home stand to travel a few hours to visit the Los Angeles Lakers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday.
 Sacramento is on a seven-game losing streak and is playing Los Angeles for the second time this month. Lakers guard Luka Dončić dropped 40 points in a 116-103 win, while rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. led the Kings with a 22-point, 12-assist double-double.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Acuff faced what he believes is the toughest player to guard in Dončić. He gets his second chance to guard the NBA's leading scorer (38.1 points per game) and try to snap a nasty losing skid in a tough gauntlet.
 Both teams have a pretty clean injury report, with only three players listed. Forwards Precious Achiuwa is doubtful with a left leg contusion, and De'Andre Hunter is questionable with left hip soreness for the Kings; guard Austin Reaves will miss his fourth straight game with a left heel contusion.
 If Achiuwa and Hunter miss Friday's game, it would be a significant blow to an already ailing frontcourt. Achiuwa bolsters the rebounding alongside Domantas Sabonis, and Hunter is the third-best volume 3-point shooter behind Leaky Black and Zach LaVine.
 The 6-foot-8 forward missed two games against the Portland Trail Blazers and Oklahoma City Thunder . Sacramento missed his hustle and presence on the boards.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He's averaging 6.4 rebounds and tallied three double-digit rebound games, including a 12-point, 10-rebound double-double.
 Hunter is making a resurgence alongside Acuff. He's two games removed from a 24-point performance on 7-for-13 shooting against the Trail Blazers on Friday.
 Acuff's gravity generates quality looks for Hunter at the 3-point line or cutting past a ball-watching defender for a quick finish. Shooting and defense are the ideal skill sets to surround the 19-year-old.
 Sacramento needs as much reinforcement as it can get over the next three games. The team will host the Boston Celtics and the San Antonio Spurs , with De'Aaron Fox returning to the Golden 1 Center after Friday's game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Their lone win this season came on the road. Maybe Coach Doug Christie and his squad could muster the same fight they had against the Dallas Mavericks to upset Los Angeles.
 The Lakers are coming off a 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday, snapping a nine-game winning streak. Dončić is known for his first-quarter flurries, but his team lets opponents back in games after he cools down.
